sentences.text: Eogranivora edentulata was a medium-sized basal ornithuromorph bird that lacked teeth in both its upper and lower jaws.
The fossil record shows that the first metatarsal and first toe are completely missing from this species.
This animal holds the distinction of being the oldest known seed-eating ornithuromorph bird, a title reflected in its specific name meaning "toothless" in Latin.
It was also the very first fossil bird species to receive a formal name in the year 2018.
Zheng Xiaoting, Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Wang Xiaoli, Wang Yan, and Zhou Zhonghe named and described the species in 2018 based on the holotype specimen STM35-3.
The holotype was found in the Yixian Formation in present-day China, dating to the Early Cretaceous between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
Scientists interpret the combination of a seed-filled crop, gastroliths, and a toothless beak as a specialization for eating seeds.
The loss of the first toe is hypothesized to be an adaptation for a running lifestyle.
